articles.title: Skirts given star billing as Prada swerves trousers and dresses in Milan
articles.summary: Combination of Miuccia Prada with Belgian designer Raf Simons once again spins gold for fashion house. Miuccia Prada’s style formula is simple: begin with a great skirt. Her personal uniform is a knee-length skirt, A-line or pleated, most often with a plain sweater and kitten heels.
body: The Prada collection that opened Milan fashion week made a compelling case for her favourite outfit, with a skirt the star of every one of the 63 looks – no dresses, no trousers. It won the room over, so expect to see the personality skirt on a high street near you soon.

For the past six years, Miuccia Prada has shared design duties with Belgian designer Raf Simons, 20 years her junior. The arrangement was considered unusual when announced, but the house of Prada has always had a way of spinning gold from quirky ideas, and it has worked.
“She had the idea to focus on skirts this time,” Simons explained before this show. “And I said, why not make it an all-skirt show?”

She prefers skirts to dresses because “they give you room for contrast”, Mrs Prada said. “The way I think and feel is complicated, contradictory. If I wear something feminine, I want to wear something masculine too. A dress is all one idea, and we are never just one idea.”
points: Combination of Miuccia Prada with Belgian designer Raf Simons once again spins gold for fashion house.

articles.title: Why you should quit and not look back: ‘Saying yes to everything is saying no to what matters’
articles.summary: In her new book, The Case For Quitting: The Surprising Benefits of Opting Out, Lindsay Crouse discusses the costs and traps of never giving up – and how she set herself free. Lindsay Crouse used to define herself as not a quitter.
body: She went to Harvard University, where she learned to become even more high-achieving and ambitious, then landed an assistant job at the New York Times and worked her way up to become an opinion writer and producer. On the weekends, Crouse ran marathons and did endurance sports, clocking new personal bests throughout her thirties.
“My entire life was really guided by only one question: how can I go harder, and do more?” she says now over Zoom.

Over time, though, that mentality began to backfire. After having two children, Crouse started falling behind, dropping balls and losing her passion for running and writing. Something needed to change.

Now Crouse argues quitting is essential for a satisfying, successful life. She herself left her prestigious job to chase unknown risks and rewards. “We need to start viewing quitting as a tool of perseverance, rather than the enemy of it,” she said. “If we find ourselves in a hole, often we dig harder when we should just stop digging.”

articles.title: Jennifer Lopez Goes Italian Diva In Dolce & Gabbana at Vogue World 2026: Milano

The singer made a triumphant entrance at the Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, the iconic glass-roofed shopping arcade located in the heart of the city, where the fifth edition of the Vogue event took place tonight. Taking place on the first day of Milan Fashion Week, actors, musicians, models, and major figures creative industries are now gathered in one place.

While all the celebrities shone brightly at Vogue World 2026, J Lo made sure that she made an impact, wearing a black tulle gown with sequin embellishments contouring the bodice and the skirt, care of Dolce & Gabbana. As for her hairstyle and makeup, the actress opted for a pink lip that matched her blush and eyeshadow. She wore her hair loose and wavy, a choice that made her look classic yet modern.

articles.title: Machine Gun Kelly and Alex Consani Bring Sporty Eco-Chic to Vogue World Milan
articles.summary: Model and Vogue cover star Alex Consani wore a pink recycled fiberglass look by Louise Trotter for Bottega Veneta, while the artist formerly known as Machine Gun Kelly stepped out in a neon orange Byblos suit.
body: MGK is no Vogue World newcomer. After all, the singer attended the event in Los Angeles last year, donning vintage Jean Paul Gaultier for the occasion. But at Vogue World 2026: Milano, he wasn’t just sitting front row, taking in the action—he walked in the show, right behind model (and Vogue World veteran) Alex Consani.

For his Vogue World runway debut, MGK (formerly known as Machine Gun Kelly ) wore a neon orange Byblos suit and Camper shoes. (His accessory? A cigarette, which he puffed defiantly as he walked). For her look, Consani wore Bottega Veneta, namely: look 80 from Louise Trotter’s fall 2026 collection, a bubblegum pink, ankle-length dress.

MGK and Consani’s looks are part of the show’s fourth act, “The Age of Intelligence,” which highlights the convergence of craftsmanship and technological advancements and nods to Milan as a hub where research, manufacturing, design, and creativity meet. One of the products of that synergy? Italian tech fabrics.

articles.title: My New Favorite Boxed Chocolate Cake Mix Tastes Like It Came from a Bakery
articles.summary: This past summer, I attended the Summer Fancy Food Show — an expo showcasing all the new food products and trends we can expect to see in the coming months — at the Javits Center in New York City.
body: Kittylamb offers a variety of baking mixes — including chocolate and vanilla cake mixes and frosting, lemon bars, and fudgy brownies. The company was created by founder Kat, who wasn’t able to find baking mixes on grocery store shelves that met her needs, so she decided to create her own. The name is an homage to the nickname her dad gave her.

All of Kittylamb’s baking mixes are certified USDA organic. Each box comes with the ingredients separated into pouches labeled A, B, and C (so you can use them in order). There are no dyes, artificial ingredients, or preservatives you can’t pronounce.

I tried Kittylamb’s The Chocolate Cake Mix. It contains cane sugar, wheat flour (never enriched or bleached), cocoa powder, vanilla extract, baking soda, baking powder, and sea salt. I paired it with Kittylamb’s Silky Chocolate Frosting made from powdered sugar, fair trade bittersweet chocolate, cocoa butter, vanilla extract, and cocoa powder. Kittylamb’s baking mixes range in price from $7 to $15. The chocolate cake mix is $10, and the chocolate frosting mix is $9. You can buy them online or in select stores across the country.

articles.title: The Story Behind Vogue World 2026: Milano’s Mesmerizing Finale Moment
articles.summary: The grand finale spectacle of Vogue World Milan involved a constellation of more than 6,000 paper objects, released from the ceiling of the Galleria and specially designed by Jony Ive’s LoveFrom creative studio over a months-long process.
body: When envisioning the finale moment, Ive and the team set out to honor the city of Milan itself. “Milan is very special in the fact that it is a city that creates and also makes,” Ive told Vogue ahead of the event. “And I think, typically, the creation and the making have become increasingly disconnected. So Milan occupies a very special place for me.”

For the paper objects—which the team named the “LoveFrom libellula” after the Italian word for dragonfly—the British-American designer drew on a myriad of inspirations and references: nature (dragonflies, sycamore seeds), Milanese lace, Venetian tile mosaics, and the volume and grandeur of the Galleria. Each of the paper objects was folded by hand, using a single piece of paper and no glue.

The team engineered multiple prototypes of the libellula and used Codex, OpenAI’s software engineering system, to build a simulation of the Galleria and visualize what the cloud of objects would look like at different sizes and densities. They tested the release of the objects in an airplane hangar and at the Galleria itself to get a sense of the aerodynamics.

articles.title: Jennifer Lopez Hit Vogue World 2026: Milano in Dolce Vita Glam
articles.summary: “I’ve always responded to Dolce & Gabbana because it feels like they really love women through their clothes,” Lopez told Vogue earlier this year.
body: When Jennifer Lopez is in Italy, she’s in peak J.Lo form. Today, she walked the Vogue World: Milano runway (inside the famed Galleria Vittorio Emanuele II, no less!) in a look that could only be described as dolce vita from head to toe. See: the glossy hair, the perfectly manicured peach nails, and the ensemble by Dolce & Gabbana, a Lopez favorite.

Today’s character was one of drama and sophistication. Earlier in the night, she walked the Vogue World Galleria carpet in a beaded black bustier gown, paired with sheer black gloves and pointy toe shoes. She had the chance to take in the show as spectator until Act III—where a model brought her up from the crowd.
It was a moment of full Federico Fellini La Dolce Vita. Under the spotlight, Lopez danced just like Sylvia did inside the Trevi Fountain.

“The look is vintage Dolce Vita fresh and the nails are matching vibes,” celebrity nail artist T om Bachik told Vogue moments after Lopez hit the Galleria. “I used my favorite Tweezerman tools for a perfect mani, then polished Jen’s nails a High glossed Apreś peachy blush giving elegantly long fingers even beneath the gloves, so chic!”

articles.title: Apple Is Bringing Back an Apple Watch Feature It Took Away With watchOS 27
articles.summary: Typically, software updates introduce new features rather than taking them away. So, when you install watchOS 27 on your compatible Apple Watch, you probably aren't surprised to see updates like Siri AI or a step counter on the watch face.
body: As reported by 9to5Mac, Apple quietly removed the app switcher from Apple Watches with watchOS 27. As a result, users running the beta over the summer, or those who updated in September, were likely confused when double-clicking the Digital Crown: On watchOS 26 and earlier, that gesture pulls up a menu with all open apps, similar to the app switcher on iPhone. This allows you to quickly return to a previously used app without needing to dive into the "honeycomb" main app menu.

With watchOS 27, that's no longer the case. Not only is the app switcher gone, but the honeycomb app menu has been sidelined. In their place, Apple is pushing its new "Dynamic app grid." When you press the Digital Crown once, you'll see this new menu, which features the apps Siri thinks you're most likely to use. That might include recently used apps, but also apps you frequently use, even if you haven't used them in a while.
